note: SAMPLE DATA for a hackathon demo. Replace with 10 to 20 real services from your borough's council website and verify every contact detail before showing this to anyone. {borough} is replaced with the BOROUGH setting at load time.

services.name: {borough} Live Well Centre
services.description: A drop-in front door where council and community services work under one roof. No appointment needed. Staff can help with money, housing, work and health in one visit.
services.who_it_is_for: Any {borough} resident.
services.how_to_access: Drop in during opening hours. Bring any letters you have.
services.contact: Address and hours: add from the council website

services.name: {borough} Council Tax Support
services.description: Reduces the council tax bill for people on a low income. The council can also agree a payment plan for arrears and pause recovery action while a claim is checked.
services.who_it_is_for: Residents on a low income or on benefits who pay council tax.
services.how_to_access: Apply online or with help at a Live Well Centre. Call the council tax team straight away if there is a reminder or summons letter.
services.contact: Council tax team: add number from the council website

services.name: {borough} Crisis Support Scheme
services.description: Short-term help with food, energy top-ups and essential household items for people facing hardship.
services.who_it_is_for: Residents in financial crisis with no other way to meet an urgent need.
services.how_to_access: Apply through the council, often with a referral from a support worker or community organisation.

services.name: Discretionary Housing Payment
services.description: Extra money towards rent when Housing Benefit or the housing part of Universal Credit does not cover it, for example to clear arrears while a longer-term plan is made.
services.who_it_is_for: Renters who already get Housing Benefit or the housing element of Universal Credit.
services.how_to_access: Apply to the council. Bring proof of rent and income.
services.contact: Housing benefit team: add from the council website

services.name: {borough} Housing Options and Homelessness Team
services.description: Help to keep a home or find somewhere new. The council has a duty to help if someone may become homeless within 56 days.
services.who_it_is_for: Anyone who has been told to leave, has received a notice, or has nowhere safe to stay.
services.how_to_access: Contact as early as possible, ideally as soon as a notice or letter arrives. There is an out-of-hours emergency line.
services.contact: Add daytime and out-of-hours numbers from the council website

services.name: {borough} Private Sector Housing Team
services.description: Inspects privately rented homes with serious problems such as damp, mould, broken heating or unsafe wiring, and can require the landlord to fix them.
services.who_it_is_for: Private renters whose landlord has not fixed a serious problem.
services.how_to_access: Report online or by phone. Photos and dates of complaints to the landlord help.

services.name: {borough} Welfare Rights Service
services.description: Free benefit checks, help with forms, and support to challenge benefit decisions and sanctions.
services.who_it_is_for: Residents who think they are missing out on benefits or want to challenge a decision.
services.how_to_access: Referral from a support worker or self-referral by phone.

services.name: Citizens Advice {borough}
services.description: Free, independent advice on debt, benefits, housing, employment and consumer problems.
services.who_it_is_for: Anyone.
services.how_to_access: Drop in, book an appointment, or call the national Adviceline.

services.name: National Debtline
services.description: Free, confidential debt advice by phone and webchat, including help to set up a plan with creditors.
services.who_it_is_for: Anyone in England, Wales or Scotland worried about debt.
services.how_to_access: Phone or webchat.

services.name: Shelter Helpline
services.description: Free expert housing advice, including on eviction, disrepair and renters' rights.
services.who_it_is_for: Anyone with a housing problem.
services.how_to_access: Phone or webchat.

services.name: {borough} Community Food Network
services.description: Emergency food parcels and community pantries across the borough. Many also offer warm spaces and advice sessions.
services.who_it_is_for: Anyone who cannot afford food. Some sites need a referral voucher.
services.how_to_access: A support worker, GP or community organisation can issue a voucher. Some pantries are open to walk-ins.
services.contact: Add local sites from the council website

services.name: {borough} Work and Health Support (Working Well)
services.description: A dedicated coach for people whose health makes it hard to find or stay in work. Coaches help with job goals, CVs and adjustments, and can link to physiotherapy or talking therapies.
services.who_it_is_for: Residents with a health condition or disability who want to work.
services.how_to_access: Self-referral, or referral by a GP, Jobcentre work coach, employer or community organisation.

services.name: Jobcentre Plus
services.description: Universal Credit claims, work coach appointments, and help to find work. Can explain and review sanctions.
services.who_it_is_for: People claiming or needing to claim Universal Credit.
services.how_to_access: Through the Universal Credit journal or by visiting the local Jobcentre.
services.contact: Universal Credit helpline: check gov.uk for the current number

services.name: {borough} Adult and Community Learning
services.description: Free courses in English (ESOL), maths, digital skills and confidence-building, often in community venues.
services.who_it_is_for: Adults who want to build skills, including those with no qualifications.
services.how_to_access: Enrol online, by phone, or at a drop-in session.

services.name: {borough} Libraries Digital Help
services.description: Free computer and wifi use, one-to-one help getting online, and free mobile data SIMs through the National Databank for people who qualify.
services.who_it_is_for: Anyone who struggles to get online or cannot afford data.
services.how_to_access: Visit any library. No booking needed for most sessions.

services.name: NHS Talking Therapies
services.description: Free NHS support for stress, low mood, anxiety and worry, by phone, online or in person.
services.who_it_is_for: Adults registered with a GP in the area.
services.how_to_access: Self-refer online or by phone, or ask a GP.
services.contact: Search 'NHS Talking Therapies' with your borough name

services.name: Social Prescribing (via GP practice)
services.description: A link worker who spends time with the person and connects them to local groups, activities and practical help.
services.who_it_is_for: Anyone registered with a GP whose wellbeing is affected by things like isolation, money or housing.
services.how_to_access: Ask the GP practice reception for a social prescribing referral.

services.name: {borough} Carers Centre
services.description: Support for current and former carers, including benefits advice, peer groups, and help moving on after caring ends.
services.who_it_is_for: Unpaid carers and people whose caring role has recently ended.
services.how_to_access: Self-referral by phone or drop-in.

services.name: {borough} Bereavement Support Group
services.description: Peer groups and one-to-one listening support for people who have lost someone close.
services.who_it_is_for: Anyone who is grieving.
services.how_to_access: Self-referral. Groups meet weekly in community venues.

services.name: {borough} Community Groups and Befriending
services.description: Local social groups, community cafes and volunteer befrienders for people who feel lonely or want to get involved.
services.who_it_is_for: Anyone who wants more connection.
services.how_to_access: Drop in, or a connector can make an introduction.

services.name: {borough} Youth Employment Hub
services.description: Support for 16 to 24 year olds who are not in education, employment or training: careers advice, work placements, apprenticeships and help back into college.
services.who_it_is_for: Young people aged 16 to 24.
services.how_to_access: Drop in, or referral by a youth worker, school, college or Jobcentre.

services.name: {borough} Family Early Help
services.description: Voluntary support for families with children facing several pressures at once, such as money, housing, school or health worries.
services.who_it_is_for: Families with children under 18.
services.how_to_access: Families can ask directly, or a school, health visitor or community worker can refer with consent.
